items.title: Pay invoice for charging station installation
items.quote: Zahlbar innerhalb von 8 Tagen ab Rechnungsdatum ohne Abzug auf unser Konto bei der Musterbank AG.
items.computation: Invoice date (Rechnungsdatum) is 16.10.2026 (Friday). This is a private payment deadline counted under §§ 187, 188 BGB, starting the day after the invoice date (17.10.2026) since the invoice date itself is the triggering event and is not counted. Counting 8 days from 17.10.2026: 17,18,19,20,21,22,23,24 Oct -> the 8th day is Saturday, 24.10.2026. As the payer resides in NW, and the deadline falls on a Saturday, it moves to the next working day under § 193 BGB (payments to a company use the payer's own Land for holidays; no NW holiday falls in between). Next working day is Monday, 26.10.2026.

items.title: Keep invoice for statutory retention period (Bauleistung)
items.quote: Bitte bewahren Sie diese Rechnung zwei Jahre auf (§ 14b Abs. 1 Satz 5 UStG).
items.computation: Statutory retention period under § 14b Abs. 1 Satz 5 UStG for private recipients of invoices for work related to real property (here: electrical installation in a garage) is two years, running from the end of the calendar year in which the invoice was issued at the earliest, but the letter simply states 'two years' from the invoice; taking the invoice date 16.10.2026 as the practical starting point gives an end date of 16.10.2028 as the latest safe date to retain the document (exact statutory end could be later, as it runs from year-end, so this is the earliest safe reading).

warnings: The letter instructs 'two years' retention from the invoice date, but § 14b UStG actually counts from the end of the calendar year of issue, so the true statutory end date (likely 31.12.2028) may be later than the 16.10.2028 estimate given — treat the due_date for that reminder as only a lower bound, not a hard deadline.
